| IN USE UNTIL NEBULA RESTARTS: TURN IT OFF AND RESTART FIRST | Remove on a mod the game started with |
| MOVED TO THE RECYCLE BIN: {NAME} / REMOVED: {NAME} | |

A mod with its own code asks first, by name, as the Mods page shows: Allow keeps it on, Not now turns it off. On Windows, an update of a mod with a file open in another program waits and takes its place at the next start.

<a id="p-reference--in-the-log"></a>

#### In the log

`nebula.log` in the settings folder. Every line about mods starts `mods:`; a line about one mod names its `id` next.

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left out: FILE: WHY` | One file of a mod couldn't be used; the rest of the mod runs |
| `left out: FILE: the mod's file is empty` | An empty file in place of one of the game's: the game's is used (on a console it would crash or be silent) |
| `left out: NAME: it has no archive ARCHIVE` / `left out: player animation NAME: …` | An object or animation names something no mod or the game brings |
| `ID: the player has no number NAME` / `ID: the game has no tuning number KEY` | A `player_constants` or `tunables` key the game doesn't have (see [Player numbers](#p-reference-player-numbers), [Settings](#p-reference-settings)) |
| `ID: KEY is set to a number too large to hold` | A number past what the game holds (`1e999`): nothing is set |
| `the story has no KEY` | A `story` key the game doesn't have |
| `ID: the galaxy NAME is left out: it has no StageData/…` | A `galaxies` row without its stage |
| `ID: the galaxy NAME can't be added: its name clashes with one the game has` | |
| `ID: the achievement KEY waits for an event the game has not: EVENT` | See [Events](#p-reference-events) |
| `ID: the music NAME can't be added: its name is the game's` | |
| `ID: the object / sound / player animation / row … can't be added` or `can't be set` | Past what the game holds, or a name it already uses |
| `NAME started` | A plugin is running |
| `NAME not started: …` | Its code changed after it was allowed, can't be read, isn't a Nebula plugin, needs a newer Nebula, was built for another plugin interface or another version of the game |
| `the last run crashed with mods' code on: it stays off for this run` | Windows; restart to try again |
| `its shaders are for another build of Nebula: the ones it needs are built here` | A `.luma`'s shader cache is from another build; nothing is lost |
| `the mods' files could not be cooked: the game runs without them: WHY` | The game's converter failed as a whole; the game runs as it is. Report WHY with the mods you have on |
| `ID: TEXT` | Anything a plugin writes with `log` |

<a id="p-reference--in-lumalink"></a>

#### In LumaLink

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CAN'T CONVERT: This mod is for Super Mario Galaxy 2 | Its patch files name `SB4` |
| CAN'T CONVERT: These textures are for Super Mario Galaxy 2 | A pack whose files name `SB4` |
| CAN'T CONVERT: This doesn't look like a mod | Nothing in it could be used |
| good to know: FILE: empty, as the game's own is; nothing to change | Left out of the `.luma` |
| N code changes need a Nebula update or a plugin | Writes with no setting yet. Everything else works |
| named without a folder; choose your game store | A loose file: give `--game` |
| note: it doesn't name its authors | From `check`, for your information |

<a id="p-reference--lumalink-check"></a>

#### `lumalink check`

`luma.json` first, valid, with its needed fields. Every `path`, `icon`, `save.path` exists. No path leaves the file. `when` names only declared options and choices. `default` is one of its choices. Every tunable is `"<file stem>.<name>"` with a value it can take; `switches` is refused, naming each one's tunable. Every file in `files/` is a kind the game can read. Each plugin library is really for the device it's listed under. Music and progression rows make sense.

<a id="p-reference--18-questions"></a>

### 18. Questions

**Does a mod need the game's files in it?** No, and it shouldn't carry them. Name an archive as a folder and change only what's yours.

**Can two mods change the same level?** Yes, through `merge/`. A whole-file replacement goes to the higher on the list.

**A mod patched memory. Will it work?** Conversion lists what became settings and what's left over. Almost everything else in it still works.

**Can I use a Galaxy 2 mod?** No. Nebula is the first game. Its levels need Galaxy 2's objects and engine.

**Can a plugin crash the game?** Yes; it runs inside it. The stable interface refuses harmless mistakes (a null actor from `spawn` is yours to check), and the crash report names the mod.

**Can I add a new power-up model?** Yes: `add_power_up` for the rules and `play` or a hook for the look, or a file at `ObjectData/IceMario.arc` to reskin one.


<a id="p-format"></a>

<a id="p-format--the-luma-format-version-1"></a>

## The `.luma` format, version 1

A `.luma` file is one mod. It works on every version of the game, every device Nebula runs on, and every Nebula from now on.

It is a zip file with `luma.json` as its first entry. Inside are the mod's files as modders make them, not a form tied to one build of the game. Nebula prepares them for itself when the mod is first used and again whenever its own needs change, so a mod never has to be converted twice.

```
My Mod.luma
├── luma.json                  what the mod is
├── icon.png                   optional: a PNG, square looks best, 256x256 is plenty
├── pictures/                  optional: screenshots and art for the mod's page
├── layers/
│   └── base/
│       ├── files/             files by their place in the game: StageData/MyGalaxy.arc
│       ├── merge/             what it adds to files many mods share, see "Adding to shared files"
│       ├── textures/          replacement textures
│       └── movies/            replacement videos
├── save/                      optional, starting files for its own saves
└── plugins/                   optional, the mod's code, see "Plugins"
```

Any zip tool can make one. `lumalink pack` makes one from a folder and checks it. `lumalink check` checks one made any other way.

<a id="p-format--lumajson"></a>

### luma.json

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "id": "kaizo-mario-galaxy",
  "name": "Kaizo Mario Galaxy",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "game": "RMG",
  "authors": ["Someone"],
  "description": { "default": "The whole game, harder.", "ja": "ゲーム全体がより難しく。" },
  "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
  "homepage": "https://example.com/kaizo",
  "icon": "icon.png",
  "pictures": ["pictures/first-galaxy.png", "pictures/boss.png"],
  "options": [
    {
      "id": "lives",
      "name": "Lives",
      "default": "normal",
      "choices": [
        { "id": "normal", "name": "Normal" },
        { "id": "one", "name": "One health" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "layers": [
    { "path": "layers/base", "tunables": { "SkeletalFishBaby.cBreakAirBubble": false } },
    { "path": "layers/one-health", "when": { "option": { "lives": ["one"] } } },
    { "path": "layers/japan-text", "when": { "version": ["J"] } }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | yes | `1`. A later number gets a line saying a newer Nebula is needed. |
| `id` | yes | Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It says which mod this is: a file with the same `id` is an update of it. |
| `name` | yes | Text, shown to players. |
| `version` | yes | Numbers with dots: `2.1.0`. Compared number by number. |
| `game` | yes | `RMG`: Super Mario Galaxy. Any other value is another game and the mod is refused by name. |
| `versions` | no | The versions it works on, from `E` (USA), `P` (Europe), `J` (Japan), `K` (Korea), `W` (Taiwan), `C` (China). Left out: all of them. Only for a mod that truly cannot work on the others. |
| `nebula` | no | The oldest Nebula it works on: `2.1.0`. |
| `requires` | no | Names of format features it cannot work without (see "Later additions"). |
| `authors` | no | Names. |
| `description` | no | Text. |
| `license` | no | Text: a license's name (`CC-BY-4.0`, `MIT`) or its own words. Shown on the mod's page. |
| `homepage` | no | A web address starting with `https://` (or `http://`). Shown on the mod's page. |
| `icon` | no | A PNG in the file. The first picture of the mod's page. |
| `pictures` | no | PNGs in the file, shown after the icon on the mod's page, in order. The game shows the first 16. |
| `needs` | no | Other mods it needs: `[{ "id": "other", "version": "1.2.0" }]`, where `version` is the oldest that will do. |
| `conflicts` | no | Mods it can't run with: `[{ "id": "other", "below": "2.0.0" }]`. Without `below`: every version. |
| `load_after`, `load_before` | no | Ids. Where this mod goes in the player's list when first added. The player's own order then wins. |
| `options` | no | What the player can choose, in the game. |
| `layers` | yes | What the mod does. |
| `save` | no | Which saves it plays on: see "Saves". Left out: the player's normal saves. |
| `galaxies` | no | Galaxies it adds: see "Galaxies". |
| `music` | no | Tracks it adds: see "Music". |
| `event_flags` | no | Rows of the game's progression: see "The game's progression". |
| `comet_schedule` | no | Each dome's comets: see "The game's progression". |
| `text` | no | Messages of the game by id: see "Messages". |
| `plugins` | no | The mod's code: see "Plugins". |
| `achievements` | no | The mod's own achievements: see "Achievements". |
| `story` | no | Where a new file starts and where the player comes back to: see "The journey". |
| `tool` | no | What made the file. Not used by the game. |

<a id="p-format--text"></a>

#### Text

Anything shown to players is a string, or an object from language to string with a `default`:

```json
"name": { "default": "Green Stars", "ja": "グリーンスター", "fr": "Étoiles vertes" }
```

Languages: `en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `fr-CA`, `es`, `es-MX`, `de`, `it`, `nl`, `pt`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`. The game takes its own language, then the language without its region, then `default`.

<a id="p-format--layers"></a>

#### Layers

A layer is a folder and the conditions for using it. Layers apply in order; a later layer's file replaces an earlier one's. This is how one file carries everything: differences between regions, languages, devices and options are layers, not separate files.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | The layer's folder. May be left out for a layer of rows alone. |
| `tunables` | The game's tuning numbers by `"<file stem>.<name>"` (or `.<function>.<k>`, `.<function>.<call>.<k>`): a number, `true`/`false`, a list (`null` keeps a place) or `{ "option": "id" }`. The mod says `"requires": ["tunables"]`. See [settings](#p-reference-settings). A layer's `switches`, from earlier versions, is refused, naming the tunable for each. |
| `object_changes` | One of the game's objects made as another, or gone: `{ "object": "BenefitItemLifeUp", "becomes": "BenefitItemOneUp" }`, with `"in"` of `placed` (the default), `treasure_boxes` or `display_models`. See [Object changes](#p-reference--object-changes). |
| `object_classes` | New object names, each made as one of the game's: `{ "name": "Bramblet", "like": "Kuribo" }`. Its files are `ObjectData/<name>.arc`. See [tutorial 8](#p-tutorials-08-new-objects). |
| `player_constants` | How the player moves, by name: `{ "mario": {...}, "luigi": {...}, "both": {...} }`, each a number, a list (`null` keeps a place) or `{ "option": "id" }`. See [player numbers](#p-reference-player-numbers). |
| `player_animations` | New player animations from the game's or the layer's `ObjectData/MarioAnime.arc`: `{ "name": "GoldFlowerSpin", "file": "FireSpin", "rate": 1.5, "blend_frames": 3 }`. `rate` is over 0, up to 100; `blend_frames` 0 to 600. The mod says `"requires": ["player-animations"]`. |
| `sound_effects` | One of the game's sounds, by name, played from the layer's file: `{ "name": "SE_PV_JUMP_S", "file": "AudioRes/Stream/Hup.wav" }`. `@luigi` after the name for Luigi's own. |
| `stages` | Rules for stages: `{ "stage": "MyHub", "scenario": 1, "acts_as": ["AstroGalaxy"], "own_rules": true }`. See [stage rules](#p-reference-stage-rules). |
| `comet_time_limits` | Comet missions' time limits: `{ "galaxy": "BattleShipGalaxy", "mission": 4, "seconds": 150 }`. |
| `materials` | Hand-written shaders by material name: see "Hand-written shaders". |
| `text`, `story`, `galaxies`, `music`, `event_flags`, `comet_schedule` | As the same keys at the top, for this layer alone: so a galaxy, a track or a message can depend on an option or a version. |
| `when` | Conditions. All of those given must hold. Left out: always. |

A layer's folder holds `files/` (whole files, see "Files"), `merge/` (additions to shared files, see "Adding to shared files"), `textures/` and `movies/`.

`when` may hold:

| Key | Holds when |
|---|---|
| `version` | The game is one of these versions: `["E", "P"]`. |
| `language` | The player's language is one of these game folders: `["UsEnglish", "EuEnglish"]`. |
| `platform` | The device is one of `windows`, `android`, `linux`, `macos`, `ios`. |
| `option` | Each named option is set to one of its listed choices: `{ "lives": ["one"] }`. |

A `when` with a key this version of Nebula does not know is false: the layer is not used.

<a id="p-format--options"></a>

#### Options

Players choose in the game, on the Mods page, and can change their minds without the mod being converted again. Changing a choice takes effect at the next reset.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. |
| `name` | Text. |
| `description` | Text, optional. |
| `default` | A choice's `id`. |
| `choices` | Each `{ "id": ..., "name": ... }`. A choice with the id `off` is shown in the player's language and means this option adds nothing. Without one, the option has no Off. |
| `range` | A choice for each number: `{ "from": 1, "to": 20, "step": 1 }`, each choice's id being its number (counting down when `from` is the larger), at most 10001. `default` is then a number. For tunables and player numbers taken from `{ "option": "id" }`. |

An option needs `choices` or a `range`, or both.

<a id="p-format--files"></a>

#### Files

`files/` holds files at the paths the game knows them by, in any case: `files/StageData/RedBlueExGalaxy/RedBlueExGalaxyMap.arc`. New paths are new files. Files stay in the form mods use: `.arc`, `.szs`, `.bcsv`, `.bmd`, `.brstm` and the rest. Files can also be modern, turned into the game's forms when the player applies the mod: glTF models and solid ground (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.kcl.glb`), PNG textures, WAV and Ogg music, and tables as JSON (`.bcsv.json`, a zone's `jmp` tables as `.json`). See [Modern files](#p-reference--modern-files). They need no `requires`.

Text for languages the mod leaves out: if a mod sets files in some language folders and not the one being played, Nebula shows the mod's text anyway, from the same language of another region, then English, then what it has. A player can turn this off for a mod.

<a id="p-format--saves"></a>

#### Saves

```json
"save": { "mode": "own", "tag": "kaizo", "path": "save", "player_can_change": false }
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `shared`: the player's normal saves. `own`: saves of its own, starting fresh or from `path`. `copy`: saves of its own, starting from a copy of the player's, which stay untouched. |
| `tag` | Mods with the same tag share saves. Left out: the mod's `id`. |
| `path` | A folder in the file with starting files, laid out as the save folder is. |
| `player_can_change` | The player may choose between the mod's saves and normal ones on the Mods page. |

Own saves live in a folder per tag, outside the mod, so they survive updating or removing it, and a mod can't load a save from another family. Two mods wanting different saves can't run together. A mod that adds a galaxy and doesn't ask for its own saves gets them anyway: a save's shape follows the galaxy list.

<a id="p-format--shaders"></a>

#### Shaders

Nobody writes shaders for a mod, and nobody compiles them. A model's materials say what it needs: when the player applies the mod, Nebula's conversion writes each material's program text, and Nebula builds the ones it lacks on that device, once, with a progress screen. LumaLink puts no compiled programs in a `.luma`: one fits only the Nebula it was built for.

<a id="p-format--modern-files"></a>

#### Modern files

Files in a layer's `files/` can be modern ones. Nebula makes them into the game's own when it prepares the mod, under the same name with the game's ending.

| Put in | Becomes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.glb`, or `.gltf` with its files | A model, `.bmd` | glTF 2. Triangles and skins. One colour and one PNG texture per material. One metre is 100 of the game's units. A material's name is the name `materials` uses |
| `.png` | An image, `.bti` | Any size. For textures inside models, use a model or `textures/` |
| `.wav` | A music stream, `.ast` | 16-bit PCM. The file's `smpl` loop is kept; without one the whole track loops |
| `.ogg` | A music stream, `.ast` | Vorbis. `LOOPSTART` with `LOOPEND` or `LOOPLENGTH` set the loop |

A new object's model, in a folder named as its archive:

```
layers/base/files/ObjectData/MyEnemy.arc/MyEnemy.glb
```

A folder named `.arc` in `files/` changes the game's archive of that name file by file: the rest of it stays the game's.

<a id="p-format--messages"></a>

#### Messages

`text` gives words for any message of the game by its id, new or in place of the game's. Each is Text, so each can have its languages. Two mods can both add messages, which replacing the game's message files doesn't allow.

```json
"text": {
  "GalaxyName_MyGalaxy": { "default": "My Galaxy", "fr": "Ma Galaxie" },
  "GalaxyNameShort_MyGalaxy": "My Galaxy",
  "ScenarioName_MyGalaxy1": "The First Star"
}
```

A new galaxy with no `GalaxyName_` message shows an empty name.

Words may hold the game's message tags in brackets: `[wait 30]`, `[page]`, `[center]`, `[sound SE_NAME]`, `[icon 7]`, `[small]`, `[normal]`, `[large]`, `[player]`, `[color 1]`, `[tag G T u...]`; `[[` is one `[`. A new message takes the talk settings of a game message named in `like`: `"MyNpc_Hello": { "default": "Hi, [player]!", "like": "AstroGalaxy_Kinopio012" }`. See [tutorial 5](#p-tutorials-05-text).

<a id="p-format--the-journey"></a>

#### The journey

```json
"story": { "first_stage": "MyFirstGalaxy", "first_mission": 1, "hub": "MyHub", "story_scenes": false }
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `first_stage`, `first_mission` | Where a new file begins, in place of the prologue |
| `hub` | Where the player goes after a galaxy, in place of the Comet Observatory. A file with a star opens there |
| `story_scenes` | `false`: none of the game's own story scenes |

See [tutorial 16](#p-tutorials-16-total-conversion).

<a id="p-format--hand-written-shaders"></a>

#### Hand-written shaders

Most mods never need this: a model's materials get their shaders by themselves. To write one yourself, name the material in a layer and list `custom-shaders` in `requires`:

```json
"requires": ["custom-shaders"],
"layers": [{
  "path": "layers/base",
  "materials": { "WaterSurface": "layers/base/shaders/water.hlsl" }
}]
```

`lumalink shader <model>` writes the pixel program Nebula makes for each of a model's materials (a `.glb` or `.gltf` as Nebula converts it, or a `.bdl`/`.bmd`), to start from; a hand-written one takes the place of that material's plain program. The file is HLSL, one file for every device. It includes `program.hlsli` (and `program_lit.hlsli` for a lit material), as the programs Nebula generates do, and the command writes those beside it; and Nebula builds it for the device's graphics interface with a progress screen. A shader that doesn't build leaves that material undrawn, and the log says why. It applies to materials of that name in the models the mod brings: a model of the game's own has to be in the layer's `files/` for its materials to change, and `lumalink check` says when no model of the mod has a material of that name. A program has no clock: for motion, give the material an animation (a `.btk` texture matrix, [tutorial 2](#p-tutorials-02-models--a-material-that-moves)) and read its moving coordinates. Example: `examples/glowing-lantern`.

<a id="p-format--adding-to-shared-files"></a>

#### Adding to shared files

Files in `files/` can be in modern forms, turned into the game's when the player applies the mod: `.glb` and `.gltf` models and their animations, `.png` (a `.tpl` in an archive's `timg` folder, otherwise a `.bti`), `.wav` and `.ogg` streams, and `.bcsv.json` tables. See [guide.md](#p-guide).

A file in `files/` replaces the whole file: the highest mod on the player's list wins. Some files many mods need to add to, such as the game's list of effects. A layer's `merge/` folder adds to them, so every mod's additions are kept. Its paths are places in the game, going inside archives:

```
layers/base/merge/ParticleData/Effect.arc/AutoEffectList.bcsv.json     rows for a table
layers/base/merge/ParticleData/Effect.arc/ParticleNames.bcsv.json      the names of new particles
layers/base/merge/ParticleData/Effect.arc/Particles.jpc                those particles
```

A table's rows are JSON. A column is named, or written as `0x` and its hash. A column left out is zero or empty. A table merge can also take rows away and change them:

```json
{
  "remove": [ { "name": "EarthenPipe" } ],
  "change": [ { "where": { "name": "SuperSpinDriver" }, "set": { "scale_x": 2.0 } } ],
  "rows": [ { "GroupName": "MyEnemy", "UniqueName": "Smoke", "EffectName": "MyFire", "JointName": "Center" } ]
}
```

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| `remove` | Takes away every row whose columns hold all the values given |
| `change` | Sets columns (`set`) of every row matching `where` |
| `rows` | Adds rows |

They run in that order, mod by mod down the player's list. A row that matches nothing is not an error: another mod may have taken it. Two mods setting one cell: the higher on the list wins, and the Mods page shows the two overlap.

Messages merge too: `merge/MessageData/messages.json` (every language) or `merge/<Language>/MessageData/Message.arc/message.bmg.json` (one) adds talk lines and changes what follows each. See [tutorial 5](#p-tutorials-05-text--talk-new-lines-and-what-follows-them).

`Particles.jpc` holds only the new particles. Each one's number in the file is its place in `ParticleNames.bcsv.json`, starting at 0. Nebula renumbers them, and their textures, when it adds them to the game's.

<a id="p-format--galaxies"></a>

#### Galaxies

A galaxy beside the game's own is its files, `StageData/<name>/<name>Scenario.arc` and `StageData/<name>.arc`, and a row here. Everything but `name` is optional.

```json
"galaxies": [{
  "name": "MyGalaxy",
  "map_position": [-60, -100],
  "dome": 1,
  "stars_to_open": 0,
  "open_conditions": [],
  "hungry_luma": { "slot": 7, "star_bits": 400 }
}]
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Its folder's name. |
| `map_position` | Where its icon goes: `[right, up]` from the middle of its dome's page, or of the grand map if it has no dome. The page is 608 wide by 456 high. The game makes the icon itself. |
| `map_pane` | The pane in the map's layout (`MapGrandGalaxy`) that shows it. Without one, or if your layout has no such pane, it isn't on the map. |
| `dome` | The dome it belongs to, 1 to 6. |
| `stars_to_open` | Power stars it takes to open. |
| `open_conditions` | Up to three event flags that open it. |
| `hungry_luma` | A hungry Luma that opens it: placed in a level as `TicoGalaxy` with its `Obj_arg7` at `slot`. The game's are slots 0 to 6, and using one takes its place. `star_bits` is the price. |

A mod that adds a galaxy keeps its own saves: `save.mode` has to be `own` or `copy`.

<a id="p-format--music"></a>

#### Music

To replace one of the game's tracks, a layer has a file of the same name. A track of your own is a file in a layer, `files/AudioRes/Stream/MyTrack.wav` (or `.ogg`, or the game's `.ast`), and a row here.

```json
"music": [{
  "name": "MyTheme",
  "file": "AudioRes/Stream/MyTheme.wav",
  "stages": [
    { "stage": "MyGalaxy" },
    { "stage": "MyGalaxy", "scenario": 3 },
    { "stage": "MyGalaxy", "change_area": 1 }
  ]
}]
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Yours to choose. Names starting `SE_`, `BGM_`, `MBGM_`, `STM_` or `ME_` are the game's. A plugin starts a track by this name with `play_music`. |
| `file` | Its place in the game. A WAV's `smpl` chunk and an Ogg's `LOOPSTART` and `LOOPEND` comments say where it loops; without them it loops from the start. |
| `stages` | Where it plays. `scenario` is a mission, leaving it out is every mission without a row of its own. `change_area` is what a `ChangeBgmCube` in that stage starts, with its `Obj_arg1` at that number. |

A row here comes before the game's own music for that stage, comets and Bowser's fortresses included.

<a id="p-format--the-games-progression"></a>

#### The game's progression

What opens what, and what each hungry Luma costs, is a table of rows by name. A row here changes the game's row of that name, or adds a new one.

```json
"event_flags": [
  { "name": "ExOpen1CocoonExGalaxy", "kind": 3, "a": 1, "b": 0, "first": "SandClockGalaxy" },
  { "name": "StarPieceCocoonExGalaxy", "kind": 8, "a": 5, "b": 80, "first": "CocoonExGalaxy" }
],
"comet_schedule": [
  { "dome": 2, "comets": [ { "galaxy": "BattleShipGalaxy", "coins": 1 }, { "galaxy": "OceanRingGalaxy", "coins": 0 } ] }
]
```

| Kind | What the row says | `a` and `b` | `first` and `second` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | How many stars | `a`: the number | |
| 2 | A galaxy's stars to open it | | `first`: the galaxy |
| 3 | A special star was got | `a`: which star | `first`: its galaxy |
| 4 | Two other rows are both on | | `first` and `second`: the rows |
| 8 | A hungry Luma | `a`: its slot. `b`: its price | `first`: the galaxy it opens |

Where each galaxy is on the map and how many stars it takes is the table `NebulaData/GalaxyInfoTable.bcsv`, which is the one table of Nebula's a layer can replace: `layers/base/files/NebulaData/GalaxyInfoTable.bcsv` or `.bcsv.json`. To add a galaxy, use `galaxies`.

Keep these together: a mod that changes them is a different journey through the game, so it should keep its own saves.

<a id="p-format--plugins"></a>

#### Plugins

A mod's code: a native library per device, with what it needs named in [plugins.md](#p-plugins).

```json
"plugins": [{
  "api": 2,
  "binaries": { "windows-x64": "plugins/my.dll", "linux-x64": "plugins/my.so" },
  "when": { "option": { "mode": ["hard"] } }
}]
```

`api` is the plugin interface it was built for. A Nebula with an older one says it needs a newer Nebula. A device with no entry in `binaries` says the mod has no version for it, and nothing of the mod is used.

<a id="p-format--achievements"></a>

#### Achievements

A mod's own achievements, beside the game's. Each unlocks once, for good: the game keeps it in `achievements.ini` with
the game's own, under the key `mod:<mod id>/<id>`, so it stays unlocked across save files, updates of the mod, and a
mod turned off and on again. When one unlocks, the game's pop-up shows its name. The achievement board gets a Mods tab
(only while a mod on has achievements) listing each with its description, and the All tab lists them after the game's.

```json
"achievements": [
  { "id": "first-coin", "name": { "default": "Pocket Change", "ja": "はじめてのコイン" }, "description": "Collect a coin.",
    "when": { "event": "coin" } },
  { "id": "kameck", "name": "Wand Breaker", "description": "Defeat a Magikoopa.", "hidden": true,
    "when": { "event": "actor_kill", "name": "Kameck" } },
  { "id": "fifty-coins", "name": "Coin Purse", "description": "Collect 50 coins in one sitting." }
]
```

| Field | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Lower-case letters, digits and dashes, unique in the mod. Keep it for good: a new id is a new achievement, and the old one's unlock is no longer shown. |
| `name` | yes | Text, shown on the pop-up and the board. |
| `description` | no | Text: what earns it, shown on the board's card. |
| `hidden` | no | `true`: the board lists it only once it is unlocked. |
| `when` | no | The game event that unlocks it, from the list below. Without `when`, only the mod's code unlocks it. |
| `when.name` | no | Only that event with this name: the galaxy for `star_get`, the object's name for `actor_kill`, the message id for `talk_line` (the names [events](#p-reference-events) gives each event). |
| `when.value` | no | Only that event with this value: the star's number for `star_get`, the action for `player_action`. |

Events `when` can name: `frame`, `stage_frame`, `stage_start`, `player_damage`, `player_miss`, `power_up`, `coin`,
`star_bit`, `star_get`, `cutscene_start`, `cutscene_end`, `actor_appear`, `actor_kill`, `player_spin`, `player_jump`,
`player_land`, `pause`, `stage_end`, `game_save`, `power_star_appear`, `talk_line`, `talk_choice`, `cutscene_part`,
`camera_change`, `sound_start`, `effect_start`, `screen`, `actor_message`, `player_action`. Each is the
`NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_` of the same name; [events](#p-reference-events) says when it comes and what its name and value are.

Anything a single event cannot say (fifty coins, a galaxy with no damage, a time) is the mod's code: it counts what it
needs and calls `unlock_achievement(self, "fifty-coins")` (see [plugins](#p-plugins)); it returns 1 when that unlocked
it now. The game keeps the first 64 achievements of a mod; one with no name, an id that is not an id, or the id of one
before it is left out.

The `achievements` example in LumaLink's `examples` folder has three unlocked by events and one by its code.

<a id="p-format--what-the-game-says"></a>

### What the game says

A mod that can't be used stays in the list, off, with one line saying why. These lines are in the game's own text, in the player's language.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| THIS MOD NEEDS A NEWER NEBULA | `format` above what it reads, a `requires` name it lacks, or `nebula` above its version. |
| THIS MOD IS FOR SUPER MARIO GALAXY 2 | `game` is `SB4` or `SB5`. |
| THIS MOD IS FOR ANOTHER GAME | Any other `game`. |
| THIS MOD DOESN'T WORK ON THIS VERSION OF THE GAME | `versions` leaves out the version being played. |
| THIS MOD NEEDS: {NAME} | A mod in `needs` is missing, off, or can't be used. |
| THIS MOD NEEDS A NEWER VERSION OF: {NAME} | A mod in `needs` is older than it says. |
| THIS MOD CAN'T RUN WITH: {NAME} | A mod in `conflicts` is on above it in the list (of two that can't run together, the lower one is left off, whichever names the other), or a mod above it plays on another family of its own saves. |
| ANOTHER COPY OF THIS MOD IS ON: {FOLDER} | Two folders hold the same `id` (a copy made by hand): the one higher in the list is used. |
| THIS MOD HAS NO VERSION FOR THIS DEVICE | A plugin has no library for this device. |
| THIS MOD'S CODE IS FOR AN OLDER NEBULA: REBUILD IT WITH THIS NEBULA'S NEBULA_MOD_API.H | A plugin's `api` is older than the game's. |
| THIS MOD'S CODE IS OFF AFTER A CRASH. RESTART TO TRY IT AGAIN | The last run crashed while mods' code ran: this run starts without it. |
| THIS FILE IS DAMAGED | Not a zip, `luma.json` missing or not readable, or a listed path missing. |

A mod's needs, conflicts, copies and saves are worked out again whenever the player turns a mod on or off or moves one, until nothing changes: a mod that loses what it needs takes with it the mods that need it.

<a id="p-format--later-additions"></a>

### Later additions

Added since version 1 began, each with its `requires` name: `tunables`, `custom-shaders` (a layer naming a material and an HLSL file that Nebula builds for every device) and `player-animations`. Modern asset files came without one.


The format stays version 1 for as long as a change can be read safely by older games:

- A reader ignores keys it does not know.
- New keys that a mod can't work without go with a name in `requires`. A Nebula without that name refuses the mod, with the first line above, and never half-applies it.
- `format` only changes if none of this can hold.

Nebula reads every format it has ever read.

<a id="p-format--checks"></a>

### Checks

`lumalink check my-mod.luma` reports each of these:

- `luma.json` is the first entry, is valid, and has its needed fields.
- Every `path`, `icon`, `pictures` entry and `save.path` exists in the file.
- `icon` and `pictures` are PNGs of at most 8192 pixels a side and 64 MB; at most 16 pictures. Over 1024 pixels a side gets a note: the game shows a picture at most 1024 a side.
- `homepage` starts with `https://` or `http://`; `license` is text.
- Each achievement has an id (unique in the mod) and a name; its `when` names an event the game has, `when.value` is a whole number, and one without `when` is in a mod with code; at most 64.
- No path leaves the file.
- `when` names only options the file declares, and only their choices.
- `default` is one of its option's choices.
- Every tunable key is `"<file stem>.<name>"` with a number, `true`/`false`, a list or an option, and the mod requires `tunables`. A layer's `switches` is refused, naming the tunable for each.
- Every file in a layer's `files/` is a kind the game can read.


<a id="p-plugins"></a>

<a id="p-plugins--plugins"></a>

## Plugins

A plugin is a mod's own compiled code. It is a native library: a `.dll` on Windows, a `.so` on Linux and Android, a `.dylib` on a Mac. The game loads it before its first line runs and calls it directly, with nothing in between.

Most mods don't need one. Levels, models, textures, music and text are files. Write a plugin when the mod has to change what the game does.

**A plugin is not sandboxed.** It can do anything the game can do on the player's device. Nebula tells players before a mod's code first runs. Only ship code you wrote or can vouch for.

<a id="p-plugins--what-you-can-do"></a>

### What you can do

| Level | What it gives you | Survives Nebula updates |
|---|---|---|
| Stable interface | `nebula_mod_api.h`: events, the player, objects, new object kinds | Yes |
| The game's headers | Subclass `LiveActor`, call any `MR::` function, read any field | Until those headers change |
| Function hooks | Run your code in place of any game function, and call the original | As long as the function exists |

Start with the stable interface. Go further only for what it can't do.

<a id="p-plugins--the-smallest-plugin"></a>

### The smallest plugin

```c
/* One-health: any hit is the last one. */
#include <nebula_mod_api.h>

static const NebulaModApi* game;

static int32_t stage_frame(const NebulaModEventData* data, void* user) {
    (void)user;
    if (game->value(NEBULA_VALUE_LIFE) > 1) {
        game->set_value(NEBULA_SET_LIFE, 1);
    }
    return data->value;
}

NEBULA_PLUGIN_ENTRY(api, self) {
    (void)self;
    game = api;
    game->subscribe(NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_FRAME, stage_frame, 0);
}
```

Build it for every device at once:

```console
lumalink build <project>
```

`lumalink build` compiles `source/*.c` with clang and lld for all eight devices (Windows, Linux, Android and macOS,
each x64 and arm64), links no library, and lists each one in `luma.json`:

```json
"plugins": [
  { "api": 2, "binaries": { "windows-x64": "plugins/one-health-windows-x64.dll", "linux-x64": "plugins/one-health-linux-x64.so", "...": "..." } }
]
```

`--clang <path>` names the compiler when it isn't on the PATH. By hand, one device:

```console
clang --target=aarch64-linux-android24 -O2 -shared -nostdlib -ffreestanding -fno-stack-protector -fvisibility=hidden -fuse-ld=lld -fPIC -Wl,-z,defs -I <nebula>/native/include -o plugins/one-health-android-arm64.so one_health.c
```

Windows targets take `-Wl,/NOENTRY` in place of `-fPIC -Wl,-z,defs`; macOS ones take neither. There is no C library:
`game->alloc` and `game->release` give memory, `game->format` does printf's formatting. If the linker stops on
`memcpy` or `memset` (clang turns a large copy or clear into one), define it in your source.

Then `lumalink pack` checks that each library is really for the device it's listed under.

<a id="p-plugins--lumajson"></a>

### luma.json

| Key | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `api` | yes | `NEBULA_MOD_API_VERSION` when you built it. |
| `binaries` | yes | A library for each device: `windows-x64`, `windows-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `macos-arm64`, `android-arm64`, `android-x64`. |
| `when` | no | The same conditions as a layer. A plugin that only runs on one option, for example. |

A player on a device with no build sees THIS MOD HAS NO VERSION FOR THIS DEVICE.

A plugin reads the player's option with `game->option(self, "option-id")`. The answer is the choice's id.

<a id="p-plugins--events"></a>

### Events

`subscribe(event, callback, user)`, only in `nebula_plugin_start`. A callback gets the event's data and returns what to use: return `data->value` to change nothing.

| Event | When | `value` | What you return does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FRAME` | Every frame, menus too | | |
| `STAGE_FRAME` | Every frame of a stage, before objects move | | |
| `STAGE_START` | A stage starts; `name` is the stage | Its mission | |
| `PLAYER_DAMAGE` | About to lose one health | 1 | 0 refuses the hit |
| `PLAYER_MISS` | About to die | How | |
| `POWER_UP` | Power-up about to change | The new one | Used instead |
| `COIN` | Coins about to be added | How many | Added instead |
| `STAR_BIT` | Star bits about to be added | How many | Added instead |
| `STAR_GET` | A star is won; `name` is the galaxy | Its number | |
| `CUTSCENE_START`, `CUTSCENE_END` | `name` is the cutscene | | |
| `ACTOR_APPEAR`, `ACTOR_KILL` | Any object; `actor` and `name` say which | | |

An event nobody subscribed to costs the game one load and one branch.

Objects made while a stage loads are reported on the loading thread. Everything else is on the game's thread.

`player()` is null outside a stage's frame. Actors are valid until the stage ends: keep none across `STAGE_START`.

<a id="p-plugins--new-objects"></a>

### New objects

```c
static void update(NebulaActor* actor, void* user) { /* every frame */ }

static NebulaObjectClass spinner = {
    sizeof(NebulaObjectClass), "MySpinner", "MySpinner", 100.0f, 0, 0, update, 0, 0
};
game->register_object(&spinner);
```

A level then places `MySpinner` like any object, and `ObjectData/MySpinner.arc` loads with the stage. A name the game already uses takes that object's place.

`spawn(name, xyz)` makes any object during play, the mod's or the game's, on any stage: its files load if the stage hasn't them. Every call is in [REFERENCE.md](#p-reference).

<a id="p-plugins--galaxies-hungry-lumas-and-messages"></a>

### Galaxies, hungry Lumas and messages

Most mods say these in `luma.json`, with no code: see [format.md](#p-format). A plugin can too, in `nebula_plugin_start`, for what it works out when it runs:

```c
NebulaGalaxy galaxy = { sizeof(NebulaGalaxy), "MyGalaxy", "MyGalaxyPane", { 0, 0, 0 }, 0, 1 };
game->add_galaxy(&galaxy);
game->add_hungry_luma("MyGalaxy", 7, 400);
game->add_text("GalaxyName_MyGalaxy", "My Galaxy");
game->add_music("MyBossTheme", "AudioRes/Stream/MyBossTheme.wav");
game->set_stage_music("MyGalaxy", 0, "MyBossTheme");
```

<a id="p-plugins--with-the-games-headers"></a>

### With the game's headers

Include `nebula_game_sdk.h` first and use `NEBULA_GAME_PLUGIN_ENTRY`. You build with the flags the game is built with, and link against `smg_game.lib`.

```cpp
class Pulse : public LiveActor { /* written as the game's own objects are */ };

void* createPulse(const char* name) { return new Pulse(name); }

NEBULA_GAME_PLUGIN_ENTRY(api, self) {
    api->register_creator("Pulse", createPulse, nullptr);
}
```

The plugin names the exact headers it was built from. On a Nebula built from other headers it isn't started, and the log says it was built for another version of the game. Rebuild it for each Nebula update that changes them.

<a id="p-plugins--function-hooks"></a>

### Function hooks

```cpp
void (*original)(MarioActor*, u16);

void myDecLife(MarioActor* self, u16 amount) {
    original(self, amount);
}

void* target = api->find_function("?decLife@MarioActor@@QEAAXG@Z");
api->hook(target, (void*)myDecLife, (void**)&original);
```

- Only in `nebula_plugin_start`.
- On Windows x64, and on Linux and Mac on x64 and arm64. A function whose first instructions can't be moved answers -1, and so does a device that won't allow it.
- A symbol's name is the compiler's: `?decLife@MarioActor@@QEAAXG@Z` on Windows, `_ZN10MarioActor7decLifeEt` on Linux and Mac.
- Several plugins can hook one function. The last one started runs first, and each one's `original` calls the one before.
- A function the compiler put inside its callers can't be reached this way. If your hook doesn't fire, use an event, or ask for one.
- Identical functions can be merged by the linker, so a hook on one can catch another.

<a id="p-plugins--when-something-goes-wrong"></a>

### When something goes wrong

A plugin that can't start is left out, and the game's log says why:

| In the log | Why |
|---|---|
| a library it needs isn't there | It depends on a `.dll` you didn't include. |
| it was built for another version of the game | A game function it calls is gone, or the headers changed. |
| it is not for this kind of computer | The wrong build for the device. |
| it is not a Nebula plugin | It doesn't export `nebula_plugin_start`. |
| it needs a newer Nebula | It was built against a later interface. |

A plugin runs inside the game, so a crash in one takes the game down. The crash report names the plugin.

<a id="p-plugins--music-and-movies"></a>

### Music and movies

```c
game->add_music("MyBossTheme", "AudioRes/Stream/MyBossTheme.ogg");   /* in nebula_plugin_start */
game->set_stage_music("MyGalaxy", 0, "MyBossTheme");                  /* 0: every mission without its own */
game->set_area_music("MyGalaxy", 1, "MyBossTheme");                   /* what a ChangeBgmCube with Obj_arg1 1 starts */

game->play_music("MyBossTheme");                                      /* in a stage */
game->stop_music(60);

game->play_movie("MovieData/MyMovie.thp");                            /* in a stage, over the game */
game->is_movie_playing();
game->stop_movie();
```

A wrong name does nothing, and the call says so where it returns a value.

<a id="p-plugins--cutscenes"></a>

### Cutscenes

`NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_START` and `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_END` give each cutscene's name. The game's own names are in Shift-JIS. A mod's are what it placed. A cutscene itself is data: see [guide.md](#p-guide).

<a id="p-plugins--the-games-progression"></a>

### The game's progression

```c
game->set_event_flag("ExOpen1CocoonExGalaxy", 3, 1, 0, "SandClockGalaxy", NULL);

const char* const galaxies[] = { "BattleShipGalaxy", "OceanRingGalaxy" };
const int32_t coins[] = { 1, 0 };
game->set_comet_schedule(2, galaxies, coins, 2);
```

Both only in `nebula_plugin_start`, and both can be data instead: `event_flags` and `comet_schedule` in [format.md](#p-format).

<a id="p-plugins--achievements"></a>

### Achievements

A mod's achievements are listed in `luma.json` (see [format.md](#p-format)): an id, a name, a description. One that a
single event earns needs no code (`"when": { "event": "star_get" }`). For the rest, the plugin counts and unlocks:

```c
static int32_t coins;

static int32_t coin(const NebulaModEventData* data, void* user) {
    if (coins < 50 && (coins += data->value) >= 50 && NEBULA_MOD_API_HAS(game, unlock_achievement)) {
        game->unlock_achievement(me, "fifty-coins");
    }
    return data->value;
}
```

`unlock_achievement(self, id)` returns 1 when it unlocked it now, 0 when it was already unlocked or the mod has no
achievement of that id. Its pop-up shows at once; any thread may call it.

<a id="p-plugins--calls-added-later"></a>

### Calls added later

Calls are only ever added at the end of `NebulaModApi`, so a plugin keeps working on every later Nebula. On an
earlier Nebula a newer call is not there: `NEBULA_MOD_API_HAS(api, call)` is true when it is. Check it before a call
added after the oldest Nebula the mod names in `nebula`, as above.

<a id="p-plugins--building-on-linux-and-mac"></a>

### Building on Linux and Mac

```console
# the stable interface: builds anywhere
cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -fvisibility=hidden -o plugins/my.so source/plugin.c

# with the game's headers on a Mac, whose linker wants to know where the game's functions will come from
c++ -std=gnu++17 -O2 -shared -fPIC -undefined dynamic_lookup -o plugins/my.dylib source/plugin.cpp
```

On Linux, a library's undefined functions are found when it's loaded, in the game. Name each build in `binaries`: `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `macos-arm64`.


<a id="p-reference-plugin-api"></a>

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--the-plugin-interface-call-by-call"></a>

## The plugin interface, call by call

Written from `nebula_mod_api.h` (by `tools/plugin_api_doc.py`), in its order: fields are only ever added at the end, so a plugin keeps working on later versions of Nebula. Check `game->size` before using a call newer than the oldest Nebula you support.

A null object, layout, point or name where a call needs one makes the call do nothing: it answers 0, null, or -1 where -1 means "no such". Where null means something (`find_actor`'s `name`), the call says so. Calls about the player or the stage do nothing, and answer 0 or null, between stages and on the file select screen. A number that is NaN or infinite, where a position, motion, angle, scale, time or tuning number is set, changes nothing either.

| Call | Signature |
|---|---|
| `log` | `void log(const NebulaPlugin* self, const char* text)` |
| `option` | `const char* option(const NebulaPlugin* self, const char* id)` |
| `subscribe` | `int32_t subscribe(NebulaModEvent event, NebulaModCallback callback, void* user)` |
| `register_object` | `int32_t register_object(const NebulaObjectClass* object)` |
| `register_creator` | `int32_t register_creator(const char* name, void*(*create)(const char* name), const char* archive)` |
| `hook` | `int32_t hook(void* target, void* replacement, void* * original)` |
| `find_function` | `void* find_function(const char* symbol)` |
| `player` | `NebulaActor* player(void)` |
| `get_position` | `void get_position(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)` |
| `set_position` | `void set_position(NebulaActor* actor, const float* xyz)` |
| `get_velocity` | `void get_velocity(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)` |
| `set_velocity` | `void set_velocity(NebulaActor* actor, const float* xyz)` |
| `value` | `int32_t value(NebulaModValue what)` |
| `set_value` | `void set_value(NebulaModSet what, int32_t value)` |
| `kill_player` | `void kill_player(void)` |
| `jump_player` | `void jump_player(const float* velocity)` |
| `appear` | `void appear(NebulaActor* actor)` |
| `kill` | `void kill(NebulaActor* actor)` |
| `is_dead` | `int32_t is_dead(NebulaActor* actor)` |
| `show_model` | `void show_model(NebulaActor* actor, int32_t show)` |
| `play` | `int32_t play(NebulaActor* actor, NebulaModPlay what, const char* name)` |
| `actor_name` | `const char* actor_name(NebulaActor* actor)` |
| `stage_name` | `const char* stage_name(void)` |
| `spawn` | `NebulaActor* spawn(const char* name, const float* xyz)` |
| `buttons_held` | `uint32_t buttons_held(void)` |
| `buttons_pressed` | `uint32_t buttons_pressed(void)` |
| `stick` | `void stick(float* x, float* y)` |
| `shake_camera` | `void shake_camera(void)` |
| `add_galaxy` | `int32_t add_galaxy(const NebulaGalaxy* galaxy)` |
| `add_hungry_luma` | `int32_t add_hungry_luma(const char* galaxy, int32_t slot, int32_t star_bits)` |
| `add_text` | `int32_t add_text(const char* id, const char* utf8)` |
| `add_power_up` | `int32_t add_power_up(const NebulaPowerUpClass* power_up)` |
| `get_gravity` | `void get_gravity(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)` |
| `add_music` | `int32_t add_music(const char* name, const char* file)` |
| `set_stage_music` | `int32_t set_stage_music(const char* stage, int32_t scenario, const char* name)` |
| `set_area_music` | `int32_t set_area_music(const char* stage, int32_t area, const char* name)` |
| `play_music` | `int32_t play_music(const char* name)` |
| `stop_music` | `void stop_music(int32_t frames)` |
| `play_movie` | `int32_t play_movie(const char* file)` |
| `stop_movie` | `void stop_movie(void)` |
| `is_movie_playing` | `int32_t is_movie_playing(void)` |
| `set_event_flag` | `int32_t set_event_flag(const char* name, int32_t kind, int32_t a, int32_t b, const char* first, const char* second)` |

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--what-each-does"></a>

### What each does

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--log"></a>

#### `log`

```c
void log(const NebulaPlugin* self, const char* text)
```

One line in the game's log.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--option"></a>

#### `option`

```c
const char* option(const NebulaPlugin* self, const char* id)
```

The choice a player made for one of the mod's options, by option id: its choice id. Null: no such option.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--subscribe"></a>

#### `subscribe`

```c
int32_t subscribe(NebulaModEvent event, NebulaModCallback callback, void* user)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start: `callback` runs at each `event` (NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_*), with what it's about. What it returns counts where the event says so (a hit refused, coins changed); else return data->value. 0: done.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--registerobject"></a>

#### `register_object`

```c
int32_t register_object(const NebulaObjectClass* object)
```

A class of objects levels can place by its name, run by the plugin's callbacks (NebulaObjectClass). 0: done; -1: no name, a name taken, or a class older than Nebula reads.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--registercreator"></a>

#### `register_creator`

```c
int32_t register_creator(const char* name, void*(*create)(const char* name), const char* archive)
```

`create` makes the game's own object (a NameObj) from its placed name; `archive` is loaded for it, or null.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--hook"></a>

#### `hook`

```c
int32_t hook(void* target, void* replacement, void* * original)
```

Run `replacement` in place of the game's function at `target`; `original` gets a call to what was there before it, which may be another plugin's. A function the compiler inlined everywhere can't be reached this way: use events. Windows x64, and Linux and Mac on x64 and arm64. Elsewhere, or for a function whose first instructions can't be moved, it answers -1.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--findfunction"></a>

#### `find_function`

```c
void* find_function(const char* symbol)
```

A game function by its symbol: on Windows, as dumpbin /exports names it. Null: no such function.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--player"></a>

#### `player`

```c
NebulaActor* player(void)
```

Null when no stage is running, or outside a stage's frame.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--getposition"></a>

#### `get_position`

```c
void get_position(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)
```

Where it is: x, y, z in the level's units.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setposition"></a>

#### `set_position`

```c
void set_position(NebulaActor* actor, const float* xyz)
```

It is there at once. The player is put there as after a warp; an object just moves.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--getvelocity"></a>

#### `get_velocity`

```c
void get_velocity(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)
```

How far it moves each frame: x, y, z. The player's is the game's own.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setvelocity"></a>

#### `set_velocity`

```c
void set_velocity(NebulaActor* actor, const float* xyz)
```

Its movement from now: the game's gravity and friction go on from it.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--value"></a>

#### `value`

```c
int32_t value(NebulaModValue what)
```

One of the game's numbers (NEBULA_VALUE_*). The player's are 0 with no stage running.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setvalue"></a>

#### `set_value`

```c
void set_value(NebulaModSet what, int32_t value)
```

Sets one (NEBULA_SET_*); nothing with no stage running. Life 0 or less: the player dies; more than the most: the most. A power-up: the game's (NEBULA_POWER_UP_*) or one add_power_up gave.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--killplayer"></a>

#### `kill_player`

```c
void kill_player(void)
```

The player dies, as from a fall out of the level.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--jumpplayer"></a>

#### `jump_player`

```c
void jump_player(const float* velocity)
```

The player leaves the ground with this velocity, as a spring sends them.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--appear"></a>

#### `appear`

```c
void appear(NebulaActor* actor)
```

It comes into the level (one killed, or one not yet shown): drawn, moving and touchable, as the game's appear.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--kill"></a>

#### `kill`

```c
void kill(NebulaActor* actor)
```

It leaves the level, as a beaten enemy: not drawn, moved or touched. appear brings it back.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--isdead"></a>

#### `is_dead`

```c
int32_t is_dead(NebulaActor* actor)
```

1 while it's out of the level (killed, or not yet appeared).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--showmodel"></a>

#### `show_model`

```c
void show_model(NebulaActor* actor, int32_t show)
```

Its model drawn (1) or not (0); it still moves and touches. Nothing for an object with no model. The player: his hands, face and power-up suit with it; his shadow stays.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--play"></a>

#### `play`

```c
int32_t play(NebulaActor* actor, NebulaModPlay what, const char* name)
```

1: it started. 0: the object has no such thing, or nothing to play it with.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--actorname"></a>

#### `actor_name`

```c
const char* actor_name(NebulaActor* actor)
```

The name it was made with: a placed object's is its name in the level (Kuribo); some of the game's own objects have Japanese names.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stagename"></a>

#### `stage_name`

```c
const char* stage_name(void)
```

The stage being played (EggStarGalaxy); null with none.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--spawn"></a>

#### `spawn`

```c
NebulaActor* spawn(const char* name, const float* xyz)
```

A registered object at a place. Its archive must already be loaded: a level places it, or the stage holds it. Null: it can't be made now.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--buttonsheld"></a>

#### `buttons_held`

```c
uint32_t buttons_held(void)
```

The controls held now: NEBULA_BUTTON_*, any together. 0 with no stage running.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--buttonspressed"></a>

#### `buttons_pressed`

```c
uint32_t buttons_pressed(void)
```

The controls pressed on this frame only: NEBULA_BUTTON_*.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stick"></a>

#### `stick`

```c
void stick(float* x, float* y)
```

The stick, each from -1 to 1 (either may be null).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--shakecamera"></a>

#### `shake_camera`

```c
void shake_camera(void)
```

In a stage: the camera shakes, as when something heavy lands (shake_camera_by chooses how hard).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addgalaxy"></a>

#### `add_galaxy`

```c
int32_t add_galaxy(const NebulaGalaxy* galaxy)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. 0: done; -2: the galaxy has no scenario archive (StageData/<name>/<name>Scenario.arc in the mod, StageData/<name>Scenario in the store), so it is left out; -1: anything else (its name clashes with one the game has).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addhungryluma"></a>

#### `add_hungry_luma`

```c
int32_t add_hungry_luma(const char* galaxy, int32_t slot, int32_t star_bits)
```

A hungry Luma: placed in a level as TicoGalaxy with its Arg7 at `slot`, it opens `galaxy` when fed `star_bits`. The game's own are slots 0 to 6: using one takes its place.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addtext"></a>

#### `add_text`

```c
int32_t add_text(const char* id, const char* utf8)
```

A message of the game by its id, in place of its own or new: GalaxyName_<galaxy>, ScenarioName_<galaxy><n>, a talk's id. A line of the game keeps its talk settings. The words may hold the game's message tags in brackets (nebula_text_tags.h).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addpowerup"></a>

#### `add_power_up`

```c
int32_t add_power_up(const NebulaPowerUpClass* power_up)
```

Its number, for set_value. Below 0: it can't be added.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--getgravity"></a>

#### `get_gravity`

```c
void get_gravity(NebulaActor* actor, float* xyz)
```

Which way is down for it, a unit length: on a planet that is no one axis.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addmusic"></a>

#### `add_music`

```c
int32_t add_music(const char* name, const char* file)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. A music track: `file` is its place in the game, AudioRes/Stream/MyTrack.wav (.ogg, .ast). `name` is yours to choose, not starting SE_, BGM_, MBGM_, STM_ or ME_, which are the game's. 0: done.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setstagemusic"></a>

#### `set_stage_music`

```c
int32_t set_stage_music(const char* stage, int32_t scenario, const char* name)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. What a stage plays: `scenario` is a mission, 0 for all it has no row for.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setareamusic"></a>

#### `set_area_music`

```c
int32_t set_area_music(const char* stage, int32_t area, const char* name)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. What a ChangeBgmCube in the stage starts, with its Obj_arg1 at `area`.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--playmusic"></a>

#### `play_music`

```c
int32_t play_music(const char* name)
```

In a stage: this track, a mod's or the game's by its name, in place of what's playing. 1: it started.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stopmusic"></a>

#### `stop_music`

```c
void stop_music(int32_t frames)
```

In a stage: what's playing fades out over this many frames.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--playmovie"></a>

#### `play_movie`

```c
int32_t play_movie(const char* file)
```

In a stage: a movie over the game, by its place in the game: MovieData/MyMovie.thp. The game waits while it plays. 1: it started.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stopmovie"></a>

#### `stop_movie`

```c
void stop_movie(void)
```

The movie playing ends now; the game goes on.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--ismovieplaying"></a>

#### `is_movie_playing`

```c
int32_t is_movie_playing(void)
```

1 while a movie plays.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--seteventflag"></a>

#### `set_event_flag`

```c
int32_t set_event_flag(const char* name, int32_t kind, int32_t a, int32_t b, const char* first, const char* second)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. A row of the game's progression, by its name: what opens what, and what each hungry Luma costs. A name the game has is changed, a new one added. `kind`: 1 stars, 2 a galaxy's stars, 3 a special star, 4 two flags, 5 story, 6 a galaxy, 7 a comet, 8 a hungry Luma. `a` and `b` follow the kind: the star's number, or the Luma's slot and its price. 0: done.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setcometschedule"></a>

#### `set_comet_schedule`

```c
int32_t set_comet_schedule(int32_t dome, const char* const* galaxies, const int32_t* coins, int32_t count)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. A dome's comets (domes 1 to 6 are the game's; 7, 8 and on add domes while they run on unbroken), in the order they come, for the whole of its schedule: `galaxies[i]` with `coins[i]` at 1 for the hundred purple coins.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setobjectchange"></a>

#### `set_object_change`

```c
int32_t set_object_change(int32_t where, const char* object, const char* becomes)
```

One of the game's objects becomes another, or (`becomes` null) is gone. Where: NEBULA_OBJECTS_*. Before stages load.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setcomettimelimit"></a>

#### `set_comet_time_limit`

```c
int32_t set_comet_time_limit(const char* galaxy, int32_t mission, int32_t seconds)
```

A comet mission's time limit in seconds, for a galaxy and mission of the player's comets.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--isanimationdone"></a>

#### `is_animation_done`

```c
int32_t is_animation_done(NebulaActor* actor)
```

An object's skeleton animation (what play's NEBULA_PLAY_ANIMATION started): 1 once it has reached its end, 0 while it plays on.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--animationframe"></a>

#### `animation_frame`

```c
float animation_frame(NebulaActor* actor)
```

Its frame now, from 0; 0 with no model.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--animationlength"></a>

#### `animation_length`

```c
float animation_length(NebulaActor* actor)
```

Its last frame; 0 with no model.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setanimationframe"></a>

#### `set_animation_frame`


```c

```

An object of register_object's own step in what it's doing: a number of the plugin's own (its enum of steps), starting at 0; state_frames counts from the set_state that began it.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--state"></a>

#### `state`

```c
int32_t state(NebulaActor* actor)
```

Its state: what set_state set last, 0 before that or for an object not register_object's.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stateframes"></a>

#### `state_frames`

```c
int32_t state_frames(NebulaActor* actor)
```

Frames since that set_state, from 0.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--nerve"></a>

#### `nerve`

```c
const char* nerve(NebulaActor* actor)
```

The game's own objects (and screens, and the states objects hand their work to) run one nerve at a time: Kuribo walks in "Kuribo.Walk". A nerve's name is "<class>.<nerve>", as docs/modding/NERVES.md lists every one. nerve: the object's now; null for one without nerves (register_object's objects have set_state). nerve_frames: its frames in it, from 0. set_nerve: it goes to another nerve of the class its nerve now is of, from its next frame (the game's code of that nerve runs, as when the game sets it). 0: done; -1: no such nerve of its class.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--nerveframes"></a>

#### `nerve_frames`

```c
int32_t nerve_frames(NebulaActor* actor)
```

Its frames in the nerve, from 0.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setnerve"></a>

#### `set_nerve`

```c
int32_t set_nerve(NebulaActor* actor, const char* nerve)
```

It goes to another nerve of its class (as nerve names it) from its next frame. 0: done; -1: no such nerve.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--hooknerve"></a>

#### `hook_nerve`

```c
int32_t hook_nerve(const char* nerve, NebulaNerveCallback callback, void* user)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. `callback` runs for every object in the nerve: as it enters, every frame of it, and as it leaves. 0: done; -1: no such nerve.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--nerveat"></a>

#### `nerve_at`

```c
const char* nerve_at(int32_t index)
```

The index-th nerve's name, for listing them all. Null: past the last.

register_object's objects: the way it faces, standing against gravity. Its model then turns with this, not with its rotation.

register_object's objects: whether anything can touch it, and hurting the player.

register_object's objects: a column of its row in the level, by the column's name, as a level editor shows it: Obj_arg0 to Obj_arg7 (-1 where the level sets none), CommonPath_ID, ShapeModelNo, CameraSetId, MessageId, GroupId, ClippingGroupId, DemoGroupId, ViewGroupId, CastId, ParentID, the SW_ columns, l_id... placement_number: 1 and the number for a number column (whole or not); 0 for a column the row lacks or one of words, or an object the level didn't place (spawn). placement_text: a column of words (name), or null.

In a stage: the game's information box (at the top, or the middle with `centre` 1) shows a message by its id (the game's or add_text's), else these words (with the game's message tags; lines wrap between words). It stays until hide_message. Asked for while the stage starts, it appears when the player has control.


The information box goes.

A sound by its name, played from a file (AudioRes/Stream/Boom.wav, .ogg, .ast): a new name, or one of the game's (SE_OJ_COIN_GET) to replace it wherever it plays, by name or by number (the player's voices, SE_PV_*). "<name>@luigi": in its place while Luigi plays. 0: done.


The star-choosing screen of a galaxy, as a launch star opens it.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setstory"></a>

#### `set_story`

```c
int32_t set_story(const char* key, const char* value)
```

Only in nebula_plugin_start. The game's journey: "first_stage" (and "first_mission", a number as text) is where a new file begins, in place of the prologue; "hub" is where the player goes after a galaxy, in place of the Comet Observatory; "story_scenes" "off" leaves out the game's own story scenes. 0: done.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--savegame"></a>

#### `save_game`

```c
void save_game(void)
```

The game writes the save, as it does after a star.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--settunable"></a>

#### `set_tunable`

```c
int32_t set_tunable(const char* key, double value)
```

A file's tuning number by "<file stem>.<name>" ("GameRules.cPlayerHealth"), or a list's place by "<file stem>.<name>[<i>]", as luma.json's "tunables" set them. Any time; most are read when an object starts, so the host sets luma.json's before the first stage. Whole kinds round and clamp. 0: done; -1: no such number.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--tunableat"></a>

#### `tunable_at`

```c
int32_t tunable_at(int32_t index, const char* * file, const char* * name, int32_t* place, int32_t* kind, double* game_value, double* value)
```

The index-th tuning number (a list counts each place): its file ("Kuribo.cpp"), name, place in its list (-1: one number), kind (1 f32, 2 f64, 3 s32, 4 u32, 5 s16, 6 u16, 7 s8, 8 u8, 9 bool), the game's number and the number now. 0: done; -1: past the last.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setgravityscale"></a>

#### `set_gravity_scale`

```c
void set_gravity_scale(float scale)
```

The game's rules as a plugin changes them, any time. Each holds until set again; a stage change keeps it. How hard gravity pulls: the player's fall and every object's. 1 the game's, 0.5 half, 0 none; below 0 pulls away.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--gravityscale"></a>

#### `gravity_scale`

```c
float gravity_scale(void)
```

The scale now.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--timer"></a>

#### `timer`

```c
int32_t timer(float* seconds_left, float* seconds_limit)
```

The countdown on the screen (a comet's time limit). 1 while one runs, with its seconds left and its whole length; 0 when none does.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--settimer"></a>

#### `set_timer`

```c
int32_t set_timer(float seconds_left)
```

Its seconds left, within its length. 0: done; -1: no countdown runs.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--pausetimer"></a>

#### `pause_timer`

```c
void pause_timer(int32_t paused)
```

1 holds every countdown where it is, 0 lets them run.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setcamera"></a>

#### `set_camera`

```c
void set_camera(const float* position, const float* target, float fov)
```

The camera at `position` looking at `target`, with `fov` degrees from the picture's top to its bottom. A null point or a fov of 0 leaves that to the game; all three left: the game's camera again. A position set is where the camera is that frame, with no easing, and it passes through walls.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--camerafov"></a>

#### `camera_fov`

```c
float camera_fov(void)
```

The angle of view the camera drew with last, in degrees.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--showhud"></a>

#### `show_hud`

```c
void show_hud(uint32_t parts, int32_t show)
```

HUD parts (NEBULA_HUD_*) hidden (0) or shown as the game shows them (1).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setgamespeed"></a>

#### `set_game_speed`

```c
void set_game_speed(float speed)
```

The scene's speed: 1 the game's, 0.5 one step every other frame, 0 held (menus and the HUD still run). Between 0 and 1. Set in a STAGE_FRAME callback, it counts from that frame.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--stepgame"></a>

#### `step_game`

```c
void step_game(int32_t steps)
```

While held: the scene runs this many steps, one a frame.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--drawtext"></a>

#### `draw_text`

```c
int32_t draw_text(int32_t line, float x, float y, float size, uint32_t rgba, const char* utf8)
```

A line of text over the game, in the game's message font. `line`: its slot, 0-15. x, y: its top-left corner, 0 to 1 across and down the screen. `size`: its height, of the screen's height (0.04 reads like the HUD's numbers). `rgba`: its colour, 0xRRGGBBAA. Null or "" takes the line away; it stays until then, across stages. 0: done; -1: no such slot.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addtextlike"></a>

#### `add_text_like`

```c
int32_t add_text_like(const char* id, const char* utf8, const char* like_id)
```

As add_text, and a new line takes the talk (camera, sound, talk and balloon type) of the game's message `like_id`; null or "": add_text. The words may hold the game's message tags in brackets ([wait 30], [color 1], [player]...: nebula_text_tags.h), as add_text's may.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--addplayeranimation"></a>

#### `add_player_animation`

```c
int32_t add_player_animation(const char* name, const char* file, float rate, int32_t blend_frames)
```

A player animation: `name` plays the bck `file` of the player's animations (ObjectData/MarioAnime.arc: the game's or one the mod adds there, a .bck or an animation in a .glb), at `rate` (1: the bck's own speed), blended in over `blend_frames` frames (0: the game's 6). Played by name (NEBULA_PLAY_PLAYER_ANIMATION), and where the game plays that name: a name the game has (its own animation table's) is played from the mod's bck. Called from the plugin's entry, before the first stage: 0 done; -1 a bad name or file, or too late.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--alloc"></a>

#### `alloc`

```c
void* alloc(uint64_t bytes)
```

Memory of the plugin's own, from the game's C library: a plugin built with none (as one built for every device is) has no malloc. alloc: null for 0 bytes or when none is left; the memory is aligned for any type. release(null) does nothing. Kept until released; a plugin's memory is never moved or reused under it.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--release"></a>

#### `release`

```c
void release(void* memory)
```

Memory of the plugin's own, from the game's C library: a plugin built with none (as one built for every device is) has no malloc. alloc: null for 0 bytes or when none is left; the memory is aligned for any type. release(null) does nothing. Kept until released; a plugin's memory is never moved or reused under it.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--format"></a>

#### `format`

```c
int32_t format(char* buffer, uint64_t size, const char* format, ...)
```

printf's formatting into `buffer` of `size` bytes, always ended with a 0 when size is above 0: what snprintf returns (the length the whole text needs; below 0 for a bad format).

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--setcameranear"></a>

#### `set_camera_near`

```c
void set_camera_near(float distance)
```

The camera's near plane in units: nothing closer to the camera is drawn. 0: the game's (100; 10 in its own first-person view). Kept until set again.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--unlockachievement"></a>

#### `unlock_achievement`

```c
int32_t unlock_achievement(const NebulaPlugin* self, const char* id)
```

One of the mod's achievements (its luma.json "achievements", by id) is unlocked: 1 now, 0 when it was already or the mod has none of that id. Its pop-up shows; the board keeps it under Mods.

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--nebulamodevent"></a>

#### `NebulaModEvent`

```c
    /* Every frame, in any scene: menus too. player() is null here. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_FRAME = 0,
    /* Every frame of a stage, before its objects move. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_FRAME,
    /* A stage has started. name: the stage. value: the mission. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_START,
    /* The player is about to lose one health. Return 0 to refuse the hit. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_DAMAGE,
    /* The player is about to die. value: how (0 a fall out of the level). Return -1 to refuse it: the player lives on where
       they are, so move them somewhere safe (set_position) and give back life (set_value) as the plugin's rule says. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_MISS,
    /* The player's power-up is about to change. value: the new one (NEBULA_POWER_UP_*); what you return is used. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_UP,
    /* Coins are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_COIN,
    /* Star bits are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_BIT,
    /* A star has been won. name: the galaxy. value: the star's number. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_GET,
    /* A cutscene starts or ends. name: the cutscene. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_START,
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_END,
    /* Any object appears or dies. actor: the object. name: its name. Subscribing to these costs a call per object. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_APPEAR,
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_KILL,
    /* The player's spin starts. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_SPIN,
    /* The player leaves the ground in a jump; lands. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_JUMP,
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_LAND,
    /* The pause menu opens or closes. value: 1 open, 0 closed. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PAUSE,
    /* The stage is ending: every actor and layout of it goes after this. name: the stage. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_END,
    /* The game is about to write the save. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_GAME_SAVE,
    /* A power star comes into the stage. value: its number. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_STAR_APPEAR,
    /* A line of talk opens in its balloon. actor: who talks. name: the line's message id, as luma.json "text" and
       add_text name it (null for a line with no id). */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_LINE,
    /* The player answered a talk's yes/no question. value: 1 yes, 0 no. actor: who asked. name: the question's
       message id. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_CHOICE,
    /* A part of a cutscene starts. value: the part's number in the cutscene, from 0. name: the part, as the
       cutscene's time sheet names it. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_PART,
    /* The camera changes. value: 0 an area's camera (also when the last event camera ends and the area's takes the view
       back), 1 an event camera (a cutscene's, a talk's, start_camera's). name: its id, as the stage's camera table names it. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CAMERA_CHANGE,
    /* A sound effect is about to start. value: its number; name: its name. What you return plays: that number, another
       sound's, or -1 for none. Subscribing costs a call per sound. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SOUND_START,
    /* An object starts one of its effects. actor: the object. name: the effect, as the object's effect table names
       it. Subscribing costs a call per effect. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_EFFECT_START,
    /* A screen layout (a counter, a menu, a message box) is shown or goes away. value: 1 shown, 0 gone. name: its
       name in the game's code. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SCREEN,
    /* An object gets a message from another: an attack, a stomp, a push, a grab (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the
       numbers). actor: who gets it. name: its name. value: the message. Return -1 to refuse it: the object acts as if
       it never came. Subscribing costs a call per message. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_MESSAGE,
    /* The player starts an action of their own: a swim, a hang, a slide, a fall (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the
       numbers). value: the action. */
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_ACTION,
    NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_COUNT
```

<a id="p-reference-plugin-api--nebulaobjectclass"></a>

#### `NebulaObjectClass`

```c
    uint32_t size;
    const char* name;
    const char* archive; /* its model and animations: ObjectData/<archive>.arc. Null: nothing to see */
    float radius;        /* what it touches with */
    void* user;
    void (*start)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
    void (*update)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
    void (*touch_player)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
    /* The player attacked it. Return 1 if it took the attack. */
    int32_t (*attacked)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
    /* The same, saying how: NEBULA_ATTACK_*. If set, it's called in place of `attacked`. */
    int32_t (*attacked_by)(NebulaActor* actor, int32_t how, void* user);
    /* What follows may be left out of an older plugin's class: `size` says. */
    int32_t kind;         /* NEBULA_OBJECT_*: how it touches things and where it's drawn */
    int32_t collision;    /* 1: its archive's collision model is solid, and moves with it */
    float shadow_radius;  /* a round shadow under it; 0: none */
    float clip_radius;    /* not run or drawn when off screen past this; 0: always */
    void (*appeared)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
    void (*killed)(NebulaActor* actor, void* user);
```
