<a id="p-reference-events"></a>

<a id="p-reference-events--events"></a>

## Events

From the game's tools/modding/events_list.py, which reads the game's source and nebula_mod_api.h.

A plugin subscribes in `nebula_plugin_start` (`game->subscribe(NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_..., callback, user)`); the
callback gets the event's `actor`, `name` and `value` and returns `data->value` unless the event uses what it
returns. An event no plugin subscribes to costs the game one load and one branch.

| Event | When, and what it carries |
|---|---|
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_FRAME` | Every frame, in any scene: menus too. player() is null here. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_FRAME` | Every frame of a stage, before its objects move. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_START` | A stage has started. name: the stage. value: the mission. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_DAMAGE` | The player is about to lose one health. Return 0 to refuse the hit. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_MISS` | The player is about to die. value: how (0 a fall out of the level). Return -1 to refuse it: the player lives on where they are, so move them somewhere safe (set_position) and give back life (set_value) as the plugin's rule says. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_UP` | The player's power-up is about to change. value: the new one (NEBULA_POWER_UP_*); what you return is used. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_COIN` | Coins are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_BIT` | Star bits are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_GET` | A star has been won. name: the galaxy. value: the star's number. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_START` | A cutscene starts or ends. name: the cutscene. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_END` | A cutscene starts or ends. name: the cutscene. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_APPEAR` | Any object appears or dies. actor: the object. name: its name. Subscribing to these costs a call per object. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_KILL` | Any object appears or dies. actor: the object. name: its name. Subscribing to these costs a call per object. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_SPIN` | The player's spin starts. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_JUMP` | The player leaves the ground in a jump; lands. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_LAND` | The player leaves the ground in a jump; lands. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PAUSE` | The pause menu opens or closes. value: 1 open, 0 closed. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_END` | The stage is ending: every actor and layout of it goes after this. name: the stage. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_GAME_SAVE` | The game is about to write the save. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_STAR_APPEAR` | A power star comes into the stage. value: its number. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_LINE` | A line of talk opens in its balloon. actor: who talks. name: the line's message id, as luma.json "text" and add_text name it (null for a line with no id). |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_CHOICE` | The player answered a talk's yes/no question. value: 1 yes, 0 no. actor: who asked. name: the question's message id. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_PART` | A part of a cutscene starts. value: the part's number in the cutscene, from 0. name: the part, as the cutscene's time sheet names it. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CAMERA_CHANGE` | The camera changes. value: 0 an area's camera (also when the last event camera ends and the area's takes the view back), 1 an event camera (a cutscene's, a talk's, start_camera's). name: its id, as the stage's camera table names it. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SOUND_START` | A sound effect is about to start. value: its number; name: its name. What you return plays: that number, another sound's, or -1 for none. Subscribing costs a call per sound. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_EFFECT_START` | An object starts one of its effects. actor: the object. name: the effect, as the object's effect table names it. Subscribing costs a call per effect. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SCREEN` | A screen layout (a counter, a menu, a message box) is shown or goes away. value: 1 shown, 0 gone. name: its name in the game's code. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_MESSAGE` | An object gets a message from another: an attack, a stomp, a push, a grab (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the numbers). actor: who gets it. name: its name. value: the message. Return -1 to refuse it: the object acts as if it never came. Subscribing costs a call per message. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_ACTION` | The player starts an action of their own: a swim, a hang, a slide, a fall (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the numbers). value: the action. |

<a id="p-reference-events--messages-nebulamodeventactormessage"></a>

### Messages (NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_MESSAGE)

The game's objects talk through messages: the player's stomp on a Goomba is `ACTMES_PLAYER_TRAMPLE` sent to it.
Ranges: the player's attacks lie between `ACTMES_PLAYER_ATTACK_START` and `ACTMES_PLAYER_ATTACK_END`, enemies'
between `ACTMES_ENEMY_ATTACK_START` and `ACTMES_ENEMY_ATTACK_END`.

<a id="p-reference-objects"></a>

<a id="p-reference-objects--objects"></a>

## Objects

Every name the game can make, as a level places it or `spawn` asks for it. Written from the game's object table. `lumalink list objects` prints the names.

- **Class** is what a thing of that name is. For `object_classes`, `like` is any of these names: a new name made the same way, with its own files.
- **Archive** is `ObjectData/<archive>.arc`. Empty: it has no archive of its own, or it's chosen when placed.

<a id="p-reference-settings"></a>

<a id="p-reference-settings--game-settings-tunables"></a>

## Game settings (tunables)

Every tuning number the game has (a walk speed, a timer, a health count, thousands of them) is a **tunable**, named
after the game's source file:

| Key | Is |
|---|---|
| `"<file stem>.<name>"` | A named number: `GameRules.cPlayerHealth`, how many hits Mario takes |
| `"<file stem>.<function>.<k>"` | The k-th step count (frames) in a function: `Kuribo.exeFlatDown.1`, how long a flattened Goomba stays |
| `"<file stem>.<function>.<call>.<k>"` | The k-th number a function gives a motion, animation or reach call: `Kuribo.tryActive.isNearPlayerAnyTime.1`, how near the player a Goomba wakes |

A layer's `tunables` sets them, and the mod
says `"requires": ["tunables"]`. A value is a number, `true` or `false`, a list for a list of numbers (`null` keeps a
place), or `{ "option": "id" }` to take the number from one of the mod's number options. Where two mods set one, the mod
higher on the list wins. A plugin reads one with `get_tunable` and sets one with `set_tunable`.

```json
"requires": ["tunables"],
"layers": [{ "tunables": { "GameRules.cPlayerHealth": 6, "GameDataPlayerStatus.cMaxPlayerLeft": 999, "ScenePlayingResult.cCoinStepNum": 100 } }]
```

The whole list, with the game's value for each, is written by the game itself: start Nebula with
`--dump-tunables <file>`. `lumalink list settings` prints the game's rules below.

| Tunable | The game has | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GameRules.cPlayerHealth` | 3 | The health a player starts with, and the most before a Life Up |
| `MarioActor.cDarkCometOneHealth` | true | Daredevil comets leave the player one health |
| `MarioActor.cHitTakesAll` | false | A hit takes all the player's health |
| `GameRules.cLifeUpHealth` | 6 | The most health a Life Up gives. 0: none |
| `MarioEffect.cLowHealthWarning` | true | The warning sound at low health or air |
| `EventUtil.cDarkCometRules` | true | Daredevil comets keep their rules; false: a comet like any other |
| `GameDataPlayerStatus.cMaxPlayerLeft` | 99 | The most lives |
| `GameDataPlayerStatus.cStartingPlayerLeft` | 4 | The lives a file starts and loads with |
| `GameRules.cMaxStarBits` | 9999 | The most star bits kept in the save |
| `GameDataTemporaryInGalaxy.cMaxCarriedStarPieceNum` | 999 | The most star bits carried in a stage |
| `GameRules.cMaxCoins` | 999 | The most coins in a stage |
| `ScenePlayingResult.cCoinStepNum` | 50 | Coins for a 1-up. 0: none |
| `ScenePlayingResult.cStarPieceStepNum` | 50 | Star bits for a 1-up. 0: none |
| `ScenePlayingResult.cPurpleCoinPowerStarAppearNum` | 100 | Purple coins that bring the star |
| `MarioActor.cWaterAir` | 8 | The air the player has under water |
| `SequenceUtil.cMissStarPieceNum` | 0 | Star bits added after a miss, negative to take. -999: all lost |
| `FlipPanel.cPanelGroupSize` | 32 | How many flip panels a group holds |
| `FlipPanel.cObserverGroupSize` | 32 | The same for their observers |
| `WaterBazooka.cShotInvalidSpinKill` | false | A spin doesn't break the water bazooka's shots |
| `BossKameckBarrier.cOffsetY` | 0 | Added to Kamek's barrier's height |
| `SkeletalFishBaby.cBreakAirBubble` | true | A hit skeletal fish leaves an air bubble |
| `GameRules.cDodoryuShellOnly` | false | Dodoryu is hurt by shells alone |
| `SceneUtil.cHiddenStarTable` | true | Hidden stars take their mission from the game's table |
| `SceneUtil.cSuddenDeathDodoryu` | true | Dodoryu's one-hit run in CosmosGardenGalaxy's fourth mission |
| `GameRules.cBegomanFireProof` | false | Begomans survive fire ground |
| `KinopioAstro.cMessangerAlwaysEx` | false | The 1-up messenger always gives its larger supply |
| `KinopioAstro.sMessangerOneUpExNum` | 20 | How many 1-ups that is |

<a id="p-reference-settings--from-switches"></a>

### From `switches`

Earlier mods named these rules in a layer's `switches`. Nebula and `lumalink check` refuse `switches` now, naming the
tunable for each; LumaLink writes tunables when it converts a console mod. A switch whose sense was "no ..." is the
opposite value of its tunable: `"no_low_health_warning": 1` is `"MarioEffect.cLowHealthWarning": false`.

| Switch | Tunable |
|---|---|
| `player_health`, `life_up_health` | `GameRules.cPlayerHealth`, `GameRules.cLifeUpHealth` |
| `player_health_fixed` | `MarioActor.cDarkCometOneHealth`, opposite |
| `hit_takes_all`, `water_air` | `MarioActor.cHitTakesAll`, `MarioActor.cWaterAir` |
| `no_low_health_warning` | `MarioEffect.cLowHealthWarning`, opposite |
| `no_dark_comet_rules` | `EventUtil.cDarkCometRules`, opposite |
| `max_lives`, `starting_lives` | `GameDataPlayerStatus.cMaxPlayerLeft`, `GameDataPlayerStatus.cStartingPlayerLeft` |
| `max_star_bits`, `max_coins` | `GameRules.cMaxStarBits`, `GameRules.cMaxCoins` |
| `max_carried_star_bits` | `GameDataTemporaryInGalaxy.cMaxCarriedStarPieceNum` |
| `coins_per_one_up`, `star_bits_per_one_up`, `purple_coins_for_star` | `ScenePlayingResult.cCoinStepNum`, `.cStarPieceStepNum`, `.cPurpleCoinPowerStarAppearNum` |
| `miss_star_pieces` | `SequenceUtil.cMissStarPieceNum` (a signed number) |
| `flip_panel_group`, `flip_panel_observer_group` | `FlipPanel.cPanelGroupSize`, `FlipPanel.cObserverGroupSize` |
| `water_bazooka_shot_flag` | `WaterBazooka.cShotInvalidSpinKill` |
| `kamek_barrier_offset_y` | `BossKameckBarrier.cOffsetY` (a number now, not float bits) |
| `skeletal_fish_baby_no_bubble` | `SkeletalFishBaby.cBreakAirBubble`, opposite |
| `dodoryu_shell_only`, `begoman_fire_proof` | `GameRules.cDodoryuShellOnly`, `GameRules.cBegomanFireProof` |
| `no_hidden_star_table`, `no_sudden_death_dodoryu` | `SceneUtil.cHiddenStarTable`, `SceneUtil.cSuddenDeathDodoryu`, both opposite |
| `messenger_always_ex`, `messenger_ex_one_ups` | `KinopioAstro.cMessangerAlwaysEx`, `KinopioAstro.sMessangerOneUpExNum` |


<a id="p-reference-player-numbers"></a>

<a id="p-reference-player-numbers--player-numbers"></a>

## Player numbers

Every number in the game's table of how the player moves, by the name a layer's `player_constants` and the plugin calls use. Written from the game's sources.

```json
"player_constants": {
  "mario": { "mJumpHeight": [null, null, 60.0] },
  "luigi": { "mJumpHeight": [null, null, 45.0] },
  "both":  { "mFireModeTime": 2400 }
}
```

A number is a number; a list sets places in order, and `null` keeps the game's number at that place. Times are in frames, at 60 a second. Speeds are units a frame; a unit is a centimetre. A plugin reads and writes these with `player_constant` and `set_player_constant`, at any time.

`lumalink list player` prints the names.

<a id="p-reference-stage-rules"></a>

<a id="p-reference-stage-rules--stage-rules"></a>

## Stage rules

The game keeps many rules by a stage's name: a Bowser arena's star, a hub's counters, an ocean's swimming. A row of a layer's `stages` gives any stage those rules, or takes them away, with no code.

```json
"stages": [
  { "stage": "MyArena", "acts_as": ["KoopaBattleVs3Galaxy"] },
  { "stage": "MyHub", "acts_as": ["AstroGalaxy"] },
  { "stage": "OceanRingGalaxy", "own_rules": false },
  { "stage": "MyGalaxy", "scenario": 3, "acts_as": ["CosmosGardenGalaxy"] }
]
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stage` | The stage this row is about |
| `scenario` | One mission of it. Left out: all of them |
| `acts_as` | The stages whose rules it also plays by |
| `own_rules` | `false`: it no longer counts as itself for these rules |

A plugin says the same with `set_stage_rules`.

These are what each name brings. `lumalink list rules` prints this.

| Name | Rules |
|---|---|
| `AstroGalaxy` | The hub: counters stay up, no 1-up from star bits, Mario walks the Observatory's way, shadows as the hub's, star bits from Lumas count for the dome |
| `AstroDome` | A dome's inside: the map opens there, its pause menu |
| `LibraryRoom` | The library: a hub location |
| `PeachCastleGardenGalaxy` | The prologue's stage: its wipe, its pause menu, its shadows |
| `PeachCastleFinalGalaxy` | The ending's castle: its Toads |
| `EpilogueDemoStage` | The epilogue: no pause menu, no wipe |
| `KoopaBattleVs1Galaxy` | A Bowser arena: the grand star's fall, demo and sequence |
| `KoopaBattleVs2Galaxy` | A Bowser arena, and enemies that drop items as this one's do |
| `KoopaBattleVs3Galaxy` | The last arena: the last grand star's long sequence |
| `OceanRingGalaxy` | Swimming with a limit on how far the player can tilt; the ocean's water sound |
| `OceanPhantomCaveGalaxy` | Water bazookas as here; Syati's and the music's rules |
| `HeavensDoorGalaxy` | Planets from the start, its flip panels, its Butterflies, its pipes; fades in |
| `HeavenlyBeachGalaxy` | Water as here |
| `HellProminenceGalaxy` | Mission 5's sideways camera, the Tamakoro ball's rules |
| `CannonFleetGalaxy` | Mogu and boss music as here |
| `BattleShipGalaxy` | Boss music, and the player's fire as here |
| `ReverseKingdomGalaxy` | Boss music as here |
| `SandClockGalaxy` | The player's sand rules |
| `TriLegLv1Galaxy` | Bowser Jr.'s entrance, the player's walking on the walker |
| `CosmosGardenGalaxy` | Mission 4 is the sudden-death Dodoryu |
| `FactoryGalaxy` | Onimasu's rules, the opening's rules |
| `EggStarGalaxy` | The first opening, mission 2's star bit limit |
| `HoneyBeeKingdomGalaxy` | Its opening |
| `IceVolcanoGalaxy` | Music, wipe |
| `SkullSharkGalaxy` | Water, its steam |
| `TearDropGalaxy` | Water sphere as here |
| `TeresaMario2DGalaxy` | Fans as here |
| `FishTunnelGalaxy` | Toad as here |
| `SurfingLv1Galaxy` | The surfing race's restart |
| `SurfingLv2Galaxy` | The same, harder |


# The game's lists

<a id="p-nebula-events"></a>

<a id="p-nebula-events--events"></a>

## Events

Generated by tools/modding/events_list.py from the game's source and nebula_mod_api.h.

A plugin subscribes in `nebula_plugin_start` (`game->subscribe(NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_..., callback, user)`); the
callback gets the event's `actor`, `name` and `value` and returns `data->value` unless the event uses what it
returns. An event no plugin subscribes to costs the game one load and one branch.

| Event | When, and what it carries |
|---|---|
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_FRAME` | Every frame, in any scene: menus too. player() is null here. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_FRAME` | Every frame of a stage, before its objects move. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_START` | A stage has started. name: the stage. value: the mission. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_DAMAGE` | The player is about to lose one health. Return 0 to refuse the hit. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_MISS` | The player is about to die. value: how (0 a fall out of the level). Return -1 to refuse it: the player lives on where they are, so move them somewhere safe (set_position) and give back life (set_value) as the plugin's rule says. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_UP` | The player's power-up is about to change. value: the new one (NEBULA_POWER_UP_*); what you return is used. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_COIN` | Coins are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_BIT` | Star bits are about to be added. value: how many; what you return is added. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAR_GET` | A star has been won. name: the galaxy. value: the star's number. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_START` | A cutscene starts or ends. name: the cutscene. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_END` | A cutscene starts or ends. name: the cutscene. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_APPEAR` | Any object appears or dies. actor: the object. name: its name. Subscribing to these costs a call per object. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_KILL` | Any object appears or dies. actor: the object. name: its name. Subscribing to these costs a call per object. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_SPIN` | The player's spin starts. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_JUMP` | The player leaves the ground in a jump; lands. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_LAND` | The player leaves the ground in a jump; lands. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PAUSE` | The pause menu opens or closes. value: 1 open, 0 closed. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_STAGE_END` | The stage is ending: every actor and layout of it goes after this. name: the stage. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_GAME_SAVE` | The game is about to write the save. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_POWER_STAR_APPEAR` | A power star comes into the stage. value: its number. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_LINE` | A line of talk opens in its balloon. actor: who talks. name: the line's message id, as luma.json "text" and add_text name it (null for a line with no id). |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_TALK_CHOICE` | The player answered a talk's yes/no question. value: 1 yes, 0 no. actor: who asked. name: the question's message id. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CUTSCENE_PART` | A part of a cutscene starts. value: the part's number in the cutscene, from 0. name: the part, as the cutscene's time sheet names it. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_CAMERA_CHANGE` | The camera changes. value: 0 an area's camera (also when the last event camera ends and the area's takes the view back), 1 an event camera (a cutscene's, a talk's, start_camera's). name: its id, as the stage's camera table names it. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SOUND_START` | A sound effect is about to start. value: its number; name: its name. What you return plays: that number, another sound's, or -1 for none. Subscribing costs a call per sound. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_EFFECT_START` | An object starts one of its effects. actor: the object. name: the effect, as the object's effect table names it. Subscribing costs a call per effect. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_SCREEN` | A screen layout (a counter, a menu, a message box) is shown or goes away. value: 1 shown, 0 gone. name: its name in the game's code. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_MESSAGE` | An object gets a message from another: an attack, a stomp, a push, a grab (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the numbers). actor: who gets it. name: its name. value: the message. Return -1 to refuse it: the object acts as if it never came. Subscribing costs a call per message. |
| `NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_PLAYER_ACTION` | The player starts an action of their own: a swim, a hang, a slide, a fall (docs/modding/EVENTS.md lists the numbers). value: the action. |

<a id="p-nebula-events--messages-nebulamodeventactormessage"></a>

### Messages (NEBULA_MOD_EVENT_ACTOR_MESSAGE)

The game's objects talk through messages: the player's stomp on a Goomba is `ACTMES_PLAYER_TRAMPLE` sent to it.
Ranges: the player's attacks lie between `ACTMES_PLAYER_ATTACK_START` and `ACTMES_PLAYER_ATTACK_END`, enemies'
between `ACTMES_ENEMY_ATTACK_START` and `ACTMES_ENEMY_ATTACK_END`.

<a id="p-nebula-nerves"></a>

<a id="p-nebula-nerves--nerves"></a>

## Nerves

Generated by tools/modding/nerves_list.py from the game's source: 3630 nerves of 629 classes.

The game's objects, screens and the states objects hand their work to run one nerve at a time: Kuribo walks in
`Kuribo.Walk`, and that nerve's code (`exeWalk`) runs every frame until another nerve is set. A plugin:

- `nerve(actor)`: the name of the nerve an object is in; `nerve_frames(actor)`: its frames in it, from 0.
- `set_nerve(actor, "Kuribo.Walk")`: the object goes to another nerve of the same class from its next frame, as
  when the game sets it (its code for entering it runs).
- `hook_nerve("Kuribo.Walk", callback, user)` (in `nebula_plugin_start`): `callback` runs for every object in it,
  with `NEBULA_NERVE_ENTER` as one enters, `NEBULA_NERVE_FRAME` every frame (return 0 and the game's code for
  that frame does not run: the plugin's replaces it) and `NEBULA_NERVE_LEAVE` after the game's own end of it.
- `nerve_at(i)`: the i-th name, for listing them all at runtime.

A nerve with no hook costs nothing: the game checks one number beside it. Nerves of a state (a class that does an
object's work for a while, such as `WalkerStateWander`) name the state's class; `actor` is the object the state
works for.

<a id="p-nebula-tables"></a>

<a id="p-nebula-tables--the-games-tables"></a>

## The game's tables

Generated by tools/modding/tables_dump.py from a store of version 18: 13552 tables in 345 kinds, 7046 columns (7014 named; #hash for the rest).

A mod changes a table with a file at the table's path under a .luma layer's `merge/` folder, `<path>.json`:
`remove` (rows matching a set of columns), `change` (`where` a set of columns, `set` columns), and `rows` to add.
The path is as listed, or the game's own with its archive (`ObjectData/DemoSheet.arc/...`). A column is named as
below; `#` and a hash is a column no game code names. `<stage>`, `<object>`, `<demo>`, `<zone>` and `<language>` stand
for each one's own table of that name.

<a id="p-nebula-tunables"></a>

<a id="p-nebula-tunables--tunables"></a>

## Tunables

Generated by tools/modding/tunables_list.py from the game's source: 4874 numbers and lists, by the game's folders.

A mod sets one by its key in a luma.json layer's `"tunables"` (with `"requires": ["tunables"]`), or from a
plugin with `set_tunable`; `get_tunable` reads one. A list's place is `key[i]`. Values are the game's, as written.
`<file>.<function>.<k>` is the k-th step count (frames) in that function; `<file>.<function>.<call>.<k>` the k-th number it gives that call.
